claims.claim: **Infection is the likeliest cause** in young infants (<3 months) and neonates (<28 days corrected age), but other serious conditions can look the same at first.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Any neonate with fever (≥38°C) needs investigating and empiric IV antibiotics.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fever is not always present** — temperature may be normal or low (<36.5°C). Observation, serial examination and investigations often help. **Early senior review is essential.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **UTI is the most common bacterial infection.** Highest-risk babies: low birth weight or premature, known medical condition (e.g. congenital anomaly), socially disadvantaged families.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ask about:** irritability, fever, lethargy or sleepiness, **poor feeding (<50% of normal over the previous 24 hours)**, **urine output (fewer than 4 wet nappies per 24 hours)**, vomiting (especially bilious), apnoea, BRUE or seizures.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Birth history:** prematurity, perinatal stress, maternal fever, maternal GBS colonisation, prolonged rupture of membranes, Apgars and resuscitation, postnatal antibiotics, vitamin K.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Also:** previous child with early onset sepsis, immunodeficiency, sick contacts, **HSV exposure**, and **high parental concern**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Behaviour and appearance are the best guide** to whether serious illness is likely.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Breathing:** tachypnoea, grunting, apnoea, hypoxia, increased work of breathing, chest deformity.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Circulation:** pallor, mottling, cyanosis; tachy- or bradycardia; **central capillary refill ≥3 seconds**; murmur, weak or reduced femoral pulses, enlarged liver; weight gain from fluid overload; hypotension.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Disability/neuro:** lethargy, irritability, poor feeding, hard to wake, no response to social cues, a cry that is weak, high-pitched or continuous, reduced tone, abnormal movements, focal signs, focal/complex/prolonged seizures.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Haematological:** bleeding, bruising, non-blanching rash. **Infection:** hypothermia or fever, bulging fontanelle, neck stiffness, **vesicular rash or encephalopathy (HSV)**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Primary HSV in the first month:** skin vesicles (absent in 1/3 of neonates, who can be afebrile), seizures or encephalopathy.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Malrotation with volvulus:** abdominal distension and bile-stained vomiting.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pyloric stenosis:** progressive, non-bilious projectile vomiting, olive mass, hypochloraemic hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis. **Intussusception:** intermittent severe pain, vomiting, pallor, lethargy, rectal bleeding (red currant stool is late).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **NEC:** abdominal distension, tenderness, vomiting, blood in stool, abdominal wall discolouration or erythema.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Congenital heart disease:** cyanosis, murmur (not always), sweating with feeds, cardiac failure, poor or absent peripheral pulses. **SVT:** persistent marked tachycardia, pallor, poor feeding.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Congenital adrenal hyperplasia:** ambiguous genitalia, dehydration, hypotension, hypoglycaemia, hyponatraemia, hyperkalaemia. **Non-accidental injury:** bruising, unexplained injury, intracranial injury, neglect.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Unwell neonate or young infant:** BGL, VBG (if available), FBE, CRP, UEC, LFT, blood culture, urine MCS (SPA).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Lumbar puncture in neonates <28 days unless contraindicated; consider it in young infants.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **By likely cause, consider** ammonia, viral swabs (e.g. HSV), ECG, and CXR, abdominal or neuroimaging.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Every seriously unwell neonate or young infant:** prompt sepsis management — **empiric antibiotics given early (IV/IM/intraosseous)**, plus aciclovir where indicated, adequate analgesia and sedation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fluids:** resuscitate as required; maintenance accounting for oral intake; **restrict to two-thirds of maintenance in meningitis or respiratory infection**; judicious in cardiac causes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Suspected bowel obstruction: nasogastric tube on free drainage.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Suspected duct-dependent congenital heart disease in a neonate: discuss early with cardiology/ICU/retrieval and consider IV prostaglandin.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Involve a senior clinician early and refer early** to paediatric, surgical or sub-specialist teams as indicated.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Recognition of the seriously unwell neonate and young infant' (Updated on May 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Recognition_of_the_seriously_unwell_neonate_and_young_infant/, retrieved 2026-09-23
